source.title: TurnBench
source.provenance: 154 dual-channel conversations; 106 speakers; six conversation types; triple annotation; ~30h evaluation corpus; associated ~104h training set
source.license_note: Gated distribution/access terms must be reviewed before commercial training; do not infer training rights from benchmark availability

findings: Human smooth turn transfers begin a median ~151 ms before the other speaker finishes
Current systems fail to reproduce anticipatory turn-taking without increased false interruptions
Backchannel-rich conversation is a major source of interruption errors
kompas_comparison: A silence/VAD-only endpointing design reacts too late for anticipatory turn transfer.
features_to_add: continuous floor projection: P(hold), P(yield), P(backchannel), P(interruption)
speculative response preparation before confirmed EOT
experiments: TurnBench-compatible causal replay
measure EOT lead/lag, false interruption rate, interruption recall, backchannel-as-interruption errors

source.title: Voice Activity Projection (VAP)
source.provenance: Turn-taking/future voice-activity projection baseline used in contemporary turn-taking evaluation
source.license_note: Verify exact code/model/data licenses for the selected implementation before redistribution or training

findings: Future voice-activity/floor projection is a stronger target than binary current voice activity for conversational turn control
Acoustic approaches can react quickly but may over-trigger; semantic approaches can be more selective but slower
kompas_comparison: Kompas should retain low-level speech activity detection but not use it as the sole floor-control signal.
features_to_add: fusion of acoustic timing and semantic completion evidence
experiments: run current endpointing and projection model in shadow mode
analyze disagreement around hesitations, continuers and clause boundaries

source.title: BayLing-Duplex
source.provenance: Full-duplex speech-language system using interleaved user audio, assistant text/audio and learned dialogue-state tokens
source.license_note: Verify repository, model-weight and training-data licenses independently before product use

findings: Learned dialogue-state tokens can decide listen/speak/continue/stop without an external VAD turn controller
Reported 92% turn-taking success and 100% interruption success on InstructS2S-Eval after full-duplex fine-tuning plus DPO
kompas_comparison: Kompas currently benefits from explicit controllable components; native learned control should first be evaluated in shadow mode rather than replacing the controller.
features_to_add: cancellable speech generation while input remains live
experiments: shadow BayLing-style learned controller against production controller
record disagreements for false barge-ins, hesitations, backchannels and true floor transfers

source.title: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment
source.provenance: Post-training method separately optimizing pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling and user interruption; evaluated on full-duplex systems including Moshi and PersonaPlex
source.license_note: Research finding; verify implementation/model/data licenses before reuse

findings: Conversational interactivity improves when pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling and interruption are optimized separately
Reported Moshi turn latency improvement from ~162 ms to ~121 ms
Semantic quality reward is needed so latency optimization does not reward irrelevant early speech
kompas_comparison: A single latency or endpoint metric is insufficient for Kompas.
features_to_add: semantic relevance guard for early response onset
experiments: score pause handling, turn-taking, backchannels and interruptions separately
plot latency-quality Pareto frontier

source.title: Instruct-FD
source.provenance: Evaluation of instruction-following for conversational turn behavior across six full-duplex systems
source.license_note: Verify benchmark data license before local redistribution/training

findings: Best reported system reached only 64.4% adherence to explicit conversational-turn instructions
Proactive backchanneling and model interruption are particularly difficult
kompas_comparison: Turn behavior should be policy-conditioned rather than encoded as one universal threshold set.
features_to_add: interaction policy layer with conservative interview, normal conversation and active coaching modes
policy controls for interruption tolerance, overlap, backchannel frequency and takeover confidence
experiments: evaluate the same utterances under multiple interaction policies
measure instruction adherence separately from acoustic correctness

source.title: DuplexChat
source.provenance: ~282,634h English + ~132,723h Japanese reconstructed speaker-separated dialogue derived from public podcasts; metadata and reconstruction/processing pipeline released rather than redistributing copyrighted podcast audio
source.license_note: Podcast source copyrights remain relevant; released pipeline/metadata does not imply unrestricted rights to train on reconstructed source audio

findings: Large-scale speaker-separated conversational data can be reconstructed from public podcast sources while keeping provenance at source level
kompas_comparison: Useful as a data-engineering reference and possible research corpus, but not automatically a commercially trainable Kompas dataset.
features_to_add: source-level provenance and rights fields for every conversational corpus
separate research/evaluation eligibility from training eligibility
experiments: sample reconstruction quality before any model training
build rights/provenance gate into dataset ingestion

source.title: Kompas Turn Dynamics Harness proposal
source.provenance: Derived from TurnBench, Full-Duplex-Bench and 2026 full-duplex dialogue findings
source.license_note: Internal derived experiment specification; benchmark licenses still govern imported benchmark data

findings: Human-like turn taking requires evaluating anticipatory yield, overlap, interruption and semantic response quality together
kompas_comparison: Existing endpoint/VAD evaluation should be expanded into causal dual-channel replay.
experiments: TurnBench first
Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5 for interruption/backchannel/background-speech cases
Full-Duplex-Bench v3 for disfluency and tool-use latency

source.title: Context-conditioned explicit speech planning
source.provenance: Derived from 2026 context-aware expressive/conversational TTS research including explicit style inference/instruction approaches
source.license_note: Internal derived feature specification; individual external models/datasets require independent license verification

findings: Expressive speech should be planned from conversational context rather than inferred only from target text
Separating style planning from acoustic realization makes behavior measurable, editable and model-agnostic
features_to_add: context window features from prior user/assistant turns
deterministic planner baseline before any learned planner
experiments: A/B/C: text-only vs generic emotion label vs context->speech_plan->synthesis
human listener contextual-appropriateness preference plus speech-native acoustic scoring

source.title: Contextual contrastive-stress evaluation
source.provenance: Derived from contextual stress benchmark findings where identical target text requires different acoustic emphasis under different preceding contexts
source.license_note: Internal derived evaluation design; external benchmark data remains subject to its own license

findings: Correct lexical emphasis is context-dependent
TTS can understand the intended stressed word yet fail to realize it acoustically
features_to_add: explicit emphasis target spans with intensity
post-synthesis acoustic verification using relative F0 excursion, duration expansion and energy change
experiments: paired contexts with identical target sentence but different required stress targets
reject indiscriminate stress by requiring both members of a pair to be correct

source.title: Kompas Speech-Native Evaluation Scorecard
source.provenance: Derived from contemporary emotional-TTS, paralinguistic and nonverbal-vocalization evaluation practice
source.license_note: Internal metric specification; imported evaluation corpora require independent license review

findings: Transcript-only correctness misses whether speech is emotionally and pragmatically appropriate
Automatic speech judges require calibration against human listening
features_to_add: speech-native evaluator with acoustic and listener-calibrated dimensions
WER/semantic correctness retained as guardrails rather than primary expressive targets
experiments: listener calibration set
automatic-vs-human rank correlation by expressive dimension

source.title: Context-conditioned nonverbal vocalization policy
source.provenance: Derived from contemporary nonverbal-vocalization benchmarks and controllable expressive-speech findings
source.license_note: Internal taxonomy/policy; external audio examples are not training-eligible until rights are verified

findings: Nonverbals function as communicative acts, not decorative audio
Type, placement, intensity and duration should be evaluated separately
features_to_add: context-conditioned sampling with hard frequency caps and anti-repetition
experiments: compare no-NV vs random-NV vs context-conditioned-NV
measure listener preference and false/inappropriate event rate

source.title: Pragmatic acoustic cue calibration
source.provenance: Derived from controlled human perception findings showing pragmatic judgments can weight acoustic cues differently from foundation-model judges
source.license_note: Internal experiment design; external study materials require license review

findings: Do not assume an audio foundation-model judge reproduces human cue weighting for sarcasm or uncertainty
Pragmatic styles need human-calibrated acoustic targets
features_to_add: separate sarcasm and uncertainty controls rather than a generic emotion label
track loudness,rate,F0 variability,pause structure and terminal contour
experiments: factorial manipulation of loudness,rate,pitch variability and pauses
fit Kompas cue weights from listener judgments rather than model priors

source.title: Speech-first language realization layer
source.provenance: Derived from speech-oriented response preference/alignment research
source.license_note: Internal deterministic realization features; no external dataset is automatically training-eligible

findings: Text optimized for reading is not always text optimized for speaking
Speech-friendly phrasing should be produced before acoustic prosody planning
features_to_add: deterministic spoken-language realization pass before speech_plan
experiments: written-style vs spoken-realized response with identical semantic content
MUSHRA-style listener comparison where practical

source.title: Kompas expressive distribution targets
source.provenance: Internal measurable feature layer built on Kompas annotated speech corpus and speech-native research
source.license_note: Internal feature specification; fit numeric distributions only from rights-cleared/local corpus

findings: Human-likeness should be represented as context-conditioned distributions rather than fixed global values
features_to_add: fit per-context distributions for WPM,F0 range,energy variation,pause duration,pause density,filled-pause rate,hesitation probability,emphasis density,laughter probability
condition by dialogue act,affect,uncertainty,turn position and interaction policy
sample within calibrated bounds with deterministic seed support
experiments: fit first on existing 389-turn annotated Kompas corpus
compare fixed defaults vs context-conditioned distribution sampling
